title: Assembler::new() allocates full buffer immediately — OOM risk on untrusted size=
description:
Assembler::new(total_size) calls vec![0u8; size] unconditionally. If the =ybegin size= field comes from an untrusted source (any article from an NNTP server), a crafted article with size=4294967295 will cause a 4 GiB allocation attempt on 64-bit targets, or an immediate OOM on 32-bit targets (caught by TotalSizeTooLarge).

On 64-bit Linux, a 16 EiB allocation will succeed in virtual address space (lazy allocation) but the actual mapped pages will grow as parts are written. However an adversary can set size= to any value up to usize::MAX and the assembler will attempt a zero-filled allocation of that size.

Fix: add a configurable maximum total_size cap (e.g. max_total_size parameter or a MAX_TOTAL_SIZE constant) and return an error if exceeded. The doc example in lib.rs shows the caller is expected to supply total_file_size — document that callers must validate it against their own resource limits before calling Assembler::new().
